# redshift_scoped_grant (Resource)

Grants scoped permissions to a user, a role, or PUBLIC. A scoped permission applies to all current and future objects of one type in a database or in a schema, for example `GRANT SELECT FOR TABLES IN SCHEMA sales DATABASE dev TO ROLE analyst`. See https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/t_scoped-permissions.html.

Scoped permissions are different from `redshift_default_privileges`. Default privileges apply only to objects that a specified user creates. Scoped permissions apply to all objects in the scope, no matter which user creates them.

This resource manages the full set of privileges for one grantee, scope, and target: applying it revokes all privileges in the scope that are not listed in `privileges`. Do not use two resources for the same grantee, scope, and target.

Limitations:

- Groups are not supported. Redshift does not accept scoped permissions for groups.
- The `functions` scope also applies to stored procedures. Redshift stores `FOR PROCEDURES` grants as `FOR FUNCTIONS` grants.
- `all` is not accepted in `privileges`. List each privilege instead.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Read access to all current and future tables in one schema
resource "redshift_scoped_grant" "analyst_tables" {
  role       = redshift_role.analyst.name
  scope      = "tables"
  schema     = "sales"
  privileges = ["select"]
}

# Without a schema, the permissions apply to all schemas in the database
resource "redshift_scoped_grant" "loader_tables" {
  user       = "loader"
  scope      = "tables"
  privileges = ["select", "insert", "update", "delete"]
}

# The functions scope also applies to stored procedures
resource "redshift_scoped_grant" "analyst_functions" {
  role       = redshift_role.analyst.name
  scope      = "functions"
  schema     = "sales"
  privileges = ["execute"]
}

# Permissions in a database other than the provider database
resource "redshift_scoped_grant" "analyst_schemas" {
  role       = redshift_role.analyst.name
  scope      = "schemas"
  database   = "reporting"
  privileges = ["usage"]
}

# Grant to PUBLIC, which includes all users
resource "redshift_scoped_grant" "public_languages" {
  public     = true
  scope      = "languages"
  privileges = ["usage"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- **privileges** (Set of String) The privileges to grant. Valid values for each scope: `schemas`: create, usage, alter, drop. `tables`: select, insert, update, delete, drop, alter, truncate, references. `functions`: execute. `languages`: usage. `copy jobs`: create, alter, drop. An empty list revokes all privileges in the scope.
- **scope** (String) The type of objects that the permissions apply to. One of: schemas, tables, functions, languages, copy jobs. The `functions` scope also applies to stored procedures.

### Optional

- **database** (String) The database that the permissions apply to. The provider connects to this database to apply the permissions, so the provider user must be able to connect to it. The default is the database of the provider when the resource is created. If you remove this attribute or change the provider database later, the permissions stay in the database where they were created.
- **id** (String) The ID of this resource.
- **public** (Boolean) Set to `true` to grant the scoped permissions to PUBLIC, which includes all users. Exactly one of `user`, `role`, or `public` must be set. Only `true` is valid. Do not set `public = false` together with `user` or `role`: Terraform counts it as a second grantee.
- **role** (String) The name of the role to grant the scoped permissions to. Exactly one of `user`, `role`, or `public` must be set. Every user or role that this role is granted to (via `redshift_role_grant`) inherits these permissions.
- **schema** (String) The schema that the permissions apply to. Valid only when `scope` is `tables` or `functions`. If you do not set it, the permissions apply to the full database.
- **user** (String) The name of the user to grant the scoped permissions to. Exactly one of `user`, `role`, or `public` must be set.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# Import with the ID <user|role|public>:<name>/<scope>/<database>[/<schema>]
# Put the ID in quotes if it contains a space, as with the "copy jobs" scope.
# Names that contain "/" can't be imported.

terraform import redshift_scoped_grant.analyst_tables role:analyst/tables/dev/sales
terraform import redshift_scoped_grant.loader_tables user:loader/tables/dev
terraform import redshift_scoped_grant.public_languages public:public/languages/dev
terraform import redshift_scoped_grant.loader_copy_jobs "user:loader/copy jobs/dev"
```
